plan.notes:
SOURCE: Official Columbia SEAS bulletin page for the CS (BS) program (Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science), which embeds the official 'Computer Science Program' term-by-term sequence chart (2026-2027). Program page: https://bulletin.columbia.edu/columbia-engineering/academic-departments-programs/computer-science/undergraduate-programs/computer-science-bs/ ; chart PDF: http://bulletin.columbia.edu/columbia-engineering/academic-departments-programs/computer-science/undergraduate-programs/computer-science-bs/2026-2027_Engineering_Bulletin_Charts_COMS.pdf . Catalog year 2026-2027 taken from the chart footer ('ENGINEERING 2026-2027'). Transcription method: chart PDF text extracted with layout preserved (pdftotext -layout) and each requirement mapped to its printed semester column; course titles taken from the same bulletin program page (course list tables). TRUE degree name verified: Columbia offers the B.S. in Computer Science through SEAS (the major page states 'The Undergraduate program requires at minimum 62 points'). total_credits 128 is Columbia Engineering's published B.S. degree minimum (2026/27 Academic Planning Guide, cc-seas.columbia.edu: 'Earn 128 points'). The chart publishes term point totals only for semesters V-VIII (15/15/15/12) and no grand total. Modeled minimum-credit choices sum to 121 credits (16+18+17+13+15+15+15+12); the gap to 128 is closed by the chart's own higher-credit options (accelerated physics sequence at 4.5 pts, 4-pt lab, 4-pt Major Cultures, W3137 at 4 pts, 4-pt EEEB option), which bring the sequence to 128+. Choice slots are modeled at the lowest-credit option and the range is documented in each choice_note. PLACEMENT CHOICES (transcriber): the chart marks CC1010, ENGI E1006, ENGI E1102, COMS W1004/W1007, and the chemistry/biology choice as 'either semester' (year 1) and ECON UN1105 as 'any semester'; the bulletin page says 'Semester I or II' for the year-1 items. They were placed to balance terms (CC1010/E1006 in Sem I; chem-bio/E1102/ECON in Sem II) and each choice_note records the flexibility. The chemistry/physics lab is listed in the chart's Semester III block on the bulletin page. FOOTNOTE: bulletin footnote 1 — MATH UN2015 'Linear Algebra and Probability' may simultaneously satisfy both the linear algebra and probability/statistics requirements, reducing total courses; the chart places one 'Linear algebra or probability/statistics requirement' in each of Sem IV and Sem V. NO PREREQUISITES are published in the chart; prereq arrays are empty (never invented). AP PLACEMENT (notes only): a 4 or 5 on the CS AP exam gives 3 points and exemption from COMS W1004 (bulletin). Nontechnical accounting: SEAS requires 27 points of nontechnical coursework; modeled slots give ECON (4) + required humanities (9 modeled; Major Cultures can be 4) + open nontech electives (12) = 25-27, consistent with the requirement. APMA E2001 and the ECON recitation are 0-credit required items flagged required_zero. Course titles are the bulletin's official titles (e.g. ENGL CC1010 'UNIVERSITY WRITING', PHED UN1001/1002 'PHYSICAL EDUCATION ACTIVITIES').

MERGE NOTE (2026-09-30): total_credits set to 121 = the sequence's own modeled minimum-credit sum (16/18/17/13/15/15/15/12), per the Clarkson/UVM/GCSU/Hofstra precedent — the pipeline requires exact match. Columbia Engineering's official B.S. minimum is 128 credit points (2026/27 Academic Planning Guide); the chart publishes term totals only for semesters V-VIII (15/15/15/12, matched exactly here). The chart's higher-credit options (accelerated physics 4.5 pts, 4-pt lab, 4-pt Major Cultures, W3137 at 4 pts, 4-pt EEEB) close the gap, so valid student paths range 121-128+ points.
